title: SDK offline debug pocket guide
body:
Purpose: quick, small reference for engineers who need to get an SDK-based client running reliably when network is flaky or fully offline (eg. field devices, pre-production demos, air-gapped sandboxes). Not a full design doc — a pragmatic checklist + minimal reproducible steps + debugging heuristics.

Audience: integrators, solutions engineers, devs building local-first demos and teams validating fallbacks before production rollout.

Key principles (short):
- Keep runtime dependency surface minimal (one tiny runtime shim and a single small storage backend).
- Telemetry must be best-effort: buffer locally, purge on policy, encrypt-at-rest if required.
- Deterministic fallbacks: predictable model downgrade path, deterministic caching rules.
- Reproducible test harness to simulate network conditions.

Quickstart (30–60m minimal loop)
1) bootstrap: clone the lightweight test harness (see linked PR above). Node runtime only; no native deps.
   - npm i @redwood/sdk-lite@canary
   - ./bin/sdk-lite init --target=local-demo
2) enable offline mode (local cache + replay): ./bin/sdk-lite config set offline true --cache=leveldb
3) simulate: ./bin/sdk-lite simulate --latency=2000 --drop=30 --mode=offline
4) run: node examples/issue-responder.js
   - Observe: SDK will first hit the local cache, then try the network when available. On failure, it will apply the fallback policy (see Fallback hierarchy).

Minimum reproducible sample (pseudo):
- SDK call shape expected: {route: string, input: string, client_id: string, seq: number, max_tokens: int} 
- Local cache key: sha256(route + client_id + prompt_prefix[:256])
- Response envelope: {status: ok|cached|error, model_id: string, tokens: int, payload: string, telemetry_events: []} 

Offline cache behaviour (recommended defaults):
- TTL: 48h for ephemeral demos, configurable per-team.
- Max items: 10k or 50MB, whichever first. Evict LRU.
- Staleness window: allow stale reads up to 5m when in strictly-offline mode, otherwise prefer fresh network if latency < 300ms.

Telemetry contract (best-effort):
- Events to record locally: request_start, request_end, fallback_triggered, cache_hit, cache_miss, replay_sent, auth_error.
- Payload size cap: 4KB per event; batch up to 20 events.
- Upload policy: attempt every 60s when network flaps; exponential backoff to 15m.
- PII: never include raw user prompt in telemetry. Hash or redact.

Fallback hierarchy (deterministic, simple):
1) Local cache hit -> return cached payload (mark telemetry cache_hit).
2) If no cache & network available -> normal call to pinned model.
3) If network available but call fails (timeout/5xx) -> retry once with reduced context length, then reduce model to a compatible lower-capacity variant (e.g. redwood-mini/compact).
4) If network unavailable -> synthetic short reply (configurable canned response) or readable error that includes retry ETA.
5) Always log fallback_triggered locally with a unique id for replay.

Smoke tests (manual):
- T0: cold start offline, first request should return canned reply and write fallback_event.
- T1: cache warming: preseed cache with a canned prompt and validate cache_hit on repeated runs.
- T2: flaky network test: start with network up, then kill network mid-request and assert deterministic downgrade path.
- T3: telemetry purge: exceed storage cap, validate oldest telemetry trimmed and critical events preserved.

Debug checklist (fast):
- Check client config: offline flag, cache path, telemetry policy.
- Inspect local cache keys/size. Leveldb CLI or sqlite browser.
- Re-run simulate with --verbose and capture sdk-lite.log. Look for "fallback_triggered" IDs.
- Reproduce: use examples/replay.js to ship stored events to staging telemetry ingestion.
- If behavior diverges between platforms (mac/linux/win): ensure Node version parity and verify leveldb binary-less mode.

Security & compliance notes (short):
- For demos with sensitive data, enable local encryption-key: ./bin/sdk-lite encrypt --kdf=scrypt --salt=random32
- Default telemetry retention: 7 days for demos, 90 days for engineering traces. Make sure to provide opt-out switches for customers.

Open questions / TODOs (short note-to-self style):
- Decide default canned response wording and per-customer customization surface.
- Agree on exact model downgrade ladder and expose as policy in SDK. (Should we add JSON policy file?)
- Add e2e test in CI that runs the simulate harness in a container.
- Confirm storage backends: LevelDB vs IndexedDB vs ephemeral FS for embedded devices. Propose matrix in follow-up doc.

References & links:
- Telemetry spec (proto): see Confluence link above.
- SDK lightweight PR: see linked PR.
- Slack channels: #devx-sdk, #solutions-demos (use traces: <fallback_id>).

Appendix: Short sample log excerpt (for quick triage)
[2026-02-12T18:12:03Z] request_start id=abc123 route=/generate client=demo-1
[2026-02-12T18:12:03Z] cache_miss id=abc123 key=0x7f4a...
[2026-02-12T18:12:05Z] network_error id=abc123 err=ETIMEDOUT
[2026-02-12T18:12:05Z] fallback_triggered id=abc123 method=reduce-context->model-compact
[2026-02-12T18:12:05Z] response_cached id=abc123 ttl=172800 size=2KB

Notes to self: keep this short for now. If adopted, expand to full spec and add sample code in Go/Rust/Python. Capture field reports from CS about demos that failed in airports (lol).

End."
